s.d: δια-τελέω, -ῶ [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 9 7|Deu.9:7]] (הָיָה), [[jeremiah 20 7|Jer.20:7, 18]] (כָּלָה), [[esther 8 13|Est.8:13]], 2Ma.5:27 * ;] prop. trans., to accomplish; used with ellipse of obj. as intrans. (Bl., § 81, 1), and joined to participles (in Ac, Lc., to adj.; see Bl., § 73, 4) with adverbial sense (= continuously), to continue: [[acts 27 33|Act.27:33.]]† (AS)
δια-τηρέω, -ῶ [in LXX for שָׁמַר, נָצַר, etc.; before ἀπό (for מִן), as in [[psalms 12 7|Psa.12:7]] (8) ;] to keep carefully: [[luke 2 51|Luk.2:51;]] before ἐκ, [[acts 15 29|Act.15:29.]]† (AS)

δια-τί , why, [[matthew 9 11|Mat.9:11, 14]] [[mark 2 18|Mrk.2:18]], [[john 7 45|Jhn.7:45]], al.; δ. τό, with inf., [[mark 5 4|Mrk.5:4]], [[luke 9 7|Luk.9:7]], [[james 4 2|Jas.4:2]]. 3. In composition, (1) through, as in διαβαίνω; (2) of separation, asunder, as in διασπάω; (3) of distribution, abroad, as in διαγγέλλω; (4) of transition, as διαλλάσσω; (5) of "perfective" action (M, Pr., 112f., 115f.), as διαφύγω, διακαθαρίζω. (AS)

δια-τίθημι [in LXX chiefly for כָּרַת, frequently δ. διαθήκην (כָּרַת) ;] to place separately, arrange, dispose. Mid, only in NT; 1. (a) in general, to dispose of; with dative of person(s), to assign to one, [[luke 22 29|Luk.22:29;]] (b) to dispose of by a will, make a testament (in cl., δ. διαθήκην also in this sense): [[hebrews 9 16|Heb.9:16-17]] (but cf. R, mg., and see: διαθήκη). 2. δ. διαθήκην, to make a covenant (Aristoph.): with dative of person(s), [[hebrews 8 10|Heb.8:10]] (LXX); before πρ, with accusative of person(s), [[acts 3 25|Act.3:25]], [[hebrews 10 16|Heb.10:16]]" (LXX) (cf. ἀντι-διατίθημι).† (AS)

δια-τρίβω [in LXX [[leviticus 14 8|Lev.14:8]] (יָשַׁב), [[jeremiah 35 7|Jer.35:7]] (גּוּר), Tob.11:8, 12, Jdth.10:2, 2Ma.14:23 * ;] to rub hard, rub away, consume; δ. χρόνον, ἡμέρας, to spend time: [[acts 14 3|Act.14:3, 28 16:12 20:6 25:6, 14]]. Intransitively with ellipse of object (El., § 81, 1), to spend time, stay: [[john 3 22|Jhn.3:22 11:54]], [[acts 15 35|Act.15:35]], [[acts 12 19|Act.12:19]].† (AS)
δια-τροφή, ῆς, ἡ (διατρέφω, to support, sustain), [in LXX: 1Ma.6:49 * ;] food, nourishment: [[1-timothy 6 8|1Ti.6:8.]]† (AS)
δι-αυγάζω [in Aq.: [[job 25 5|Job.25:5]] * ;] to shine through, to dawn: [[2-peter 1 19|2Pe.1:19]] (cf. ἕως οὗ διαπνεύσῃ ἡ ἡμέρα, [[galatians 2 17|Gal.2:17]]).† (AS)

διαφανής, -ές (διαφαίνω to show through, shine through) [in LXX: [[exodus 30 34|Exo.30:34]] (זַךְ), [[isaiah 3 22|Isa.3:22]] (גִּלָּיוֹן), [[esther 1 6|Est.1:6]] * ;] transparent: [[revelation 21 21|Rev.21:21]] (Rec.; see διαγής).† (AS)

δια-φέρω [in LXX for שְׁנָא (שְׁנָא ([[daniel 7 1|Dan.7:1-28]] only); [[1-kings 17 39|1Ki.17:39]], [[esther 3 13|Est.3:13]], al. ;] 1. trans., (a) to carry through: before διά, [[mark 11 16|Mrk.11:16;]] (b) to carry about, spread abroad: pass., [[acts 13 49|Act.13:49 27:27]]. 2. Intrans., (a) to differ: τὰ διαφέροντα, [[romans 2 18|Rom.2:18]], [[philippians 1 10|Php.1:10]] (R, mg., but see infr.); impers., διαφέρει, it makes a difference, it matters: [[galatians 2 6|Gal.2:6;]] (b) to excel: with genitive [[matthew 6 26|Mat.6:26 10:31 12:12]], [[luke 12 7|Luk.12:7, 24]], [[1-corinthians 15 41|1Co.15:41]], [[galatians 4 1|Gal.4:1]]; τὰ διαφέροντα, [[romans 2 18|Rom.2:18]], [[philippians 1 10|Php.1:10]] (R, txt.; for discussion and reff. see ICC on Ro, Phi, ll. with).† (AS)
δια-φεύγω [in LXX: [[joshua 8 22|Jos.8:22]] (פָּלִיט), [[joshua 10 28|Jos.10:28]] (שָׂרִיד), etc. ;] to flee through, escape: [[acts 27 42|Act.27:42.]]† (AS)

δια-φημίζω in late writers only, to spread abroad: τ. λόγον (= דָּבָר, the matter), [[mark 1 45|Mrk.1:45]], [[matthew 28 15|Mat.28:15]]; with accusative of person(s), to spread abroad one's fame: [[matthew 9 31|Mat.9:31.]]† (AS)

δια-φθείρω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת hi. ;] 1. to destroy utterly: [[luke 12 33|Luk.12:33]], [[revelation 11 18|Rev.11:18]]; pass., to be destroyed, disabled: [[revelation 8 9|Rev.8:9]], [[2-corinthians 4 16|2Co.4:16]]. 2. In moral sense, to corrupt, deprave: τ. γῆν, [[revelation 11 18|Rev.11:18;]] pass., διεφθαρμένοι τ. νοῦν, [[1-timothy 6 5|1Ti.6:5.]]† (AS)

δια-φθορὰ, -ᾶς, ἡ (διαφθείρω), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת, and cogn. forms ;] 1. destruction. 2. corruption (physical or moral): of the grave, [[acts 2 27|Act.2:27]] (LXX), [[acts 2 31|Act.2:31 13:34-37]].† (AS)

διά-φορος, -ον (διαφέρω), [in LXX for שְׁנָא ([[daniel 7 7|Dan.7:7, 19]]); also as in Polyb., iv, 188, al., Τὸ δ., τὰ δ., money: Sir.27:1 42:5, 2Ma.3:6 ;] 1. different: [[romans 12 6|Rom.12:6]], [[hebrews 9 10|Heb.9:10]]. 2. excellent: compar., -ώτερος, [[hebrews 1 4|Heb.1:4 8:6]].† (AS)
δια-φυλάσσω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁמַר (as [[psalms 91 11|Psa.91:11]]) ;] to guard carefully (M, Pr., 116), defend: with accusative, [[luke 4 10|Luk.4:10]] (LXX).† (AS)
δια-χειρίζω (χείρ), to have in hand, conduct, manage. Mid. (a) = act.; (b) in late writers (Polyb., FlJ, al.), to lay hands on, kill: with accusative, [[acts 5 30|Act.5:30 26:21]].† (AS)

δια-χωρίζω [in LXX: [[genesis 1 4|Gen.1:4]] ff (בָּדַל hi.), [[genesis 13 9|Gen.13:9]] ff. (פָּרַד ni.), etc. ;] to separate entirely. Mid., to separate oneself, depart: before ἀπό [[luke 9 33|Luk.9:33.]]† (AS)
διδακτικός, -ή, -όν (= cl. διδασκαλικός) apt at teaching: [[1-timothy 3 2|1Ti.3:2]], [[2-timothy 2 24|2Ti.2:24]].† (AS)

διδακτός, -ή, -όν (διδάσκω), [in LXX: [[isaiah 54 13|Isa.54:13]] (לִמּוּד), 1Ma.4:7 * ;] 1. that can be taught. 2. taught; with genitive, of source of teaching (in cl., poët. only); (a) of persons: δ. θεοῦ, [[john 6 45|Jhn.6:45]] (LXX); (b) of things, λόγοις δ. πνεύματος, [[1-corinthians 2 13|1Co.2:13.]]† (AS)

διδασκαλία, -ας, ἡ (διδάσκω), [in LXX: [[proverbs 2 17|Pro.2:17]] (אַלּוּף), [[isaiah 29 13|Isa.29:13]] (לָמַד), Sir.24:33 39:8 * ;] teaching, instruction, in both active and objective senses, most frequently the latter: [[romans 12 7|Rom.12:7 15:4]], [[ephesians 4 14|Eph.4:14]], [[1-timothy 4 6|1Ti.4:6, 13, 16 5:17 6:1, 3]], [[2-timothy 3 10|2Ti.3:10 3:16]], [[titus 2 7|Tit.2:7, 10]]; ὑγιαινοῦσα δ., [[1-timothy 1 10|1Ti.1:10]], [[2-timothy 4 3|2Ti.4:3]], [[titus 1 9|Tit.1:9 2:1]]; pl., δ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, [[colossians 2 22|Col.2:22;]] δ. δαιμονίων, [[1-timothy 4 1|1Ti.4:1]], δ. διδάσκειν, [[matthew 15 9|Mat.15:9]], [[mark 7 7|Mrk.7:7]]" (LXX) (Cremer, 182).† SYN.: διδαχή (AS)

διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ (διδάσκω), [in LXX: [[esther 6 1|Est.6:1]], 2Ma.1:10 * ;] given as rendering of Heb. רַבִּי ,רַבּוֺן (NT, Ῥαββεί, Ῥαββουνεί which see); a teacher: [[john 1 39|Jhn.1:39 20:16]]; of Jewish teachers, [[luke 2 46|Luk.2:46]], [[john 3 10|Jhn.3:10]], cf. [[romans 2 20|Rom.2:20-21;]] of John Baptist, [[luke 3 12|Luk.3:12;]] of Jesus, [[john 3 2|Jhn.3:2, 10 8:4 11:28 13:13-14]], and often in Syn., most frequently in voc., as title of address, as [[matthew 8 19|Mat.8:19]], [[mark 4 38|Mrk.4:38]]; of Jesus by himself, [[matthew 23 8|Mat.23:8;]] of an apostle, [[1-timothy 2 7|1Ti.2:7]], [[2-timothy 1 11|2Ti.1:11]]; of Christians, [[1-corinthians 12 28|1Co.12:28-29]], [[ephesians 4 11|Eph.4:11]], [[acts 13 1|Act.13:1]], [[james 3 1|Jas.3:1]]; of false teachers, [[2-timothy 4 3|2Ti.4:3]] (Cremer, 181; DB, i, 609, iii, 294, iv, 691) SYN.: παιδευτής, q.v (AS)

διδάσκω [in LXX chiefly for למד pl., also for ידע hi., ירה hi., etc. ;] to teach (i.e. instruct) a person, teach a thing; 1. trans.: with accusative of person(s), [[matthew 5 2|Mat.5:2]], [[mark 1 22|Mrk.1:22]], al.; before ὅτι, [[mark 8 31|Mrk.8:31;]] περί, [[1-john 2 27|1Jn.2:27;]] with inf., [[luke 11 1|Luk.11:1;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[mark 6 30|Mrk.6:30 12:14]]; with cogn. accusative, [[matthew 15 9|Mat.15:9]] (LXX); with dupl. accusative, [[mark 4 2|Mrk.4:2]], [[john 14 26|Jhn.14:26]]; pass., [[galatians 1 12|Gal.1:12]], [[2-thessalonians 2 15|2Th.2:15]]; with dative of person(s) (like Heb., cf. [[job 21 23|Job.21:23]], but prob. a vernac. usage, see Swete, in l.), [[revelation 2 14|Rev.2:14.]] 2. Absol., to teach, give instruction: [[matthew 4 23|Mat.4:23]], [[mark 1 21|Mrk.1:21]], and often in Gosp., [[romans 12 7|Rom.12:7]], [[1-corinthians 4 17|1Co.4:17]], [[1-timothy 2 12|1Ti.2:12]], al. SYN.: παιδεύω (cf. Westc., Heb., 402; Cremer, 180). (AS)

διδαχή, -ῆς, ἡ (διδάσκω), [in LXX: [[psalms 60 1|Psa.60:1-12]] title. (לָמַד pi.); Sm.: [[deuteronomy 33 8|Deu.33:8]] * ;] 1. objectively, teaching, doctrine, that which is taught: [[mark 1 27|Mrk.1:27]], [[john 7 16|Jhn.7:16]], [[acts 17 19|Act.17:19]], [[romans 6 7|Rom.6:7 16:17]], 2Jn.10, [[revelation 2 24|Rev.2:24]]; with genitive poss., [[matthew 7 28|Mat.7:28 16:12 22:33]], [[mark 1 22|Mrk.1:22 11:18]], [[luke 4 32|Luk.4:32]], [[john 18 19|Jhn.18:19]], [[acts 5 28|Act.5:28]], [[revelation 2 14|Rev.2:14-15]]; ἡ δ., of Christ, [[john 7 17|Jhn.7:17]], [[acts 13 12|Act.13:12]], 2Jn.9; of. τὴν δ., [[titus 1 9|Tit.1:9;]] with genitive obj., βαπτισμῶν δ., [[hebrews 6 2|Heb.6:2;]] pl., [[hebrews 13 9|Heb.13:9.]] 2. Actively, teaching: [[acts 2 42|Act.2:42]], [[2-timothy 4 2|2Ti.4:2]]; ἐν τ. δ., in the course of his teaching: [[mark 4 2|Mrk.4:2 12:38]]; λαλεῖν ἐν δ., [[1-corinthians 14 6|1Co.14:6;]] ἔχειν δ., [[1-corinthians 14 26|1Co.14:26]] (DCG, i, 485; Cremer, 181).† SYN.: διδασκαλία (AS)

δίδραχμος, -ον (δίς, δραχμή), worth two drachmae; τὸ δ. (sc. νόμισμα, coin), [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶל ([[genesis 23 15|Gen.23:15]], a1.), also for כֶּסֶף: [[genesis 20 16|Gen.20:16]], [[deuteronomy 22 29|Deu.22:29]] ;] a double drachma, nearly equal to the Jewish half-shekel, the amount of the Temple tax: [[matthew 17 24|Mat.17:24]] (DB, iii, 428).† (AS)
Δίδυμος, -ου, ὁ (prop. name from δίδυμος, -η, -ον, double, sc. παῖς, twin) Didymus, surname of the apostle Thomas: [[john 11 16|Jhn.11:16 20:24 21:2]].† (AS)

δίδωμι, [in LXX chiefly for נָתַן (53 words in all) ;] to give—in various senses, accusative to context—bestow, grant, supply, deliver, commit, yield: absol., [[acts 20 35|Act.20:35;]] with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), [[matthew 4 9|Mat.4:9 5:31]], [[john 1 12|Jhn.1:12]], al. mult.; with dative of person(s), before ἐκ, [[matthew 25 8|Mat.25:8;]] id. with genitive part.. [[revelation 2 17|Rev.2:17;]] with accusative of person(s), [[john 3 16|Jhn.3:16]], [[revelation 20 13|Rev.20:13]], al.; δεξιάς, [[galatians 2 9|Gal.2:9;]] φίλημα, [[luke 7 45|Luk.7:45;]] γνῶσιν, [[luke 1 77|Luk.1:77;]] κρίσιν, [[john 5 22|Jhn.5:22;]] of seed yielding fruit, [[mark 4 7|Mrk.4:7]], 8; ἐργασίαν (Deiss., LAE, 117f.), [[luke 12 58|Luk.12:58;]] with inf. fin., [[matthew 27 34|Mat.27:34]], [[mark 5 43|Mrk.5:43]], [[luke 8 55|Luk.8:55]], [[john 6 52|Jhn.6:52]], al.; with dative of person(s) and inf., [[luke 1 74|Luk.1:74]], al.; with accusative and inf., [[acts 2 27|Act.2:27]], [[revelation 3 9|Rev.3:9]]; with dupl. accusative, [[matthew 20 28|Mat.20:28]], [[mark 10 45|Mrk.10:45]], [[ephesians 1 22|Eph.1:22 4:11]], [[2-thessalonians 3 9|2Th.3:9]], [[1-timothy 2 6|1Ti.2:6]], al.; ἑαυτὸν δ. εἰς (Polyb., al.), [[acts 19 31|Act.19:31;]] with dative of person(s), before κατά (MM, Exp., xi), [[revelation 2 28|Rev.2:28]] (LXX); δ. ἵνα, [[revelation 3 9|Rev.3:9;]] δέδωκα ἐνώπιόν σου θύραν ἀνεῳγμένην, [[revelation 3 8|Rev.3:8.]] SYN.: δωρέομαι. (AS)

δι-εγείρω [in LXX: Jdth.1:4, [[esther 1 1|Est.1:1]], 2Ma.7:21 2Mac 15:10, 3Ma.5:15 * ;] to arouse completely, arouse as from rest or sleep: [[luke 8 24|Luk.8:24;]] pass., [[mark 4 39|Mrk.4:39]], [[luke 8 24|Luk.8:24]]; of the sea, [[john 6 18|Jhn.6:18.]] Metaphorical, of the mind: ἐν ὑπομνήσει, [[2-peter 1 13|2Pe.1:13 3:1]].† (AS)

δι-έ-οδος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹצָאָה, as [[numbers 34 4|Num.34:4]]ff, and frequently in Jos;] in π. of the conclusion of a trial (MM, Exp., xi); a way out through, an outlet; pl., δ. τῶν ὁδῶν, RV, the partings of the highways: [[matthew 22 9|Mat.22:9.]]† (AS)
δι-ερμηνευτής, -οῦ, ὁ (διερμηνεύω), an interpreter: [[1-corinthians 14 28|1Co.14:28.]]† (AS)

δι-ερμηνεύω [in LXX: 2Ma.1:36 * ;] intensive of ἐρμηνεύω, to interpret; (a) to explain, expound: with accusative, [[luke 24 27|Luk.24:27;]] absol., [[1-corinthians 12 30|1Co.12:30 14:5 14:13 14:27]]; (b) to translate: [[acts 9 36|Act.9:36.]]† (AS)

δι-έρχομαι [in LXX for אֵבֶר, הָלַךְ, בּוֹא, etc. ;] 1. to go through, pass through; (a) of things: [[matthew 19 24|Mat.19:24]], [[mark 10 25|Mrk.10:25]], [[luke 2 35|Luk.2:35]], al.; (b) of persons: [[luke 19 4|Luk.19:4;]] with accusative loc., [[luke 19 1|Luk.19:1]], [[hebrews 4 14|Heb.4:14]], [[acts 12 10|Act.12:10]]; before διά, with genitive loc., [[matthew 12 43|Mat.12:43]], [[1-corinthians 10 1|1Co.10:1]]; before εἰς, [[mark 4 35|Mrk.4:35;]] ἕως, [[luke 2 15|Luk.2:15.]] 2. to go about: [[luke 9 6|Luk.9:6]], [[acts 20 25|Act.20:25]]; of a report, to spread, go abroad (Thuc.), [[luke 5 15|Luk.5:15]] (AS)
δι-ερωτάω, -ῶ to find by inquiry: with accusative, [[acts 10 17|Act.10:17.]]† (AS)

διετής, -ές (δίς, ἔτος), [in LXX: 2Ma.10:3 * ;] 1. lasting two years. 2. two years old: ἀπὸ δ. (sc. παιδός, or neuter; cf. [[1-chronicles 27 23|1Ch.27:23]], ἀπὸ εἰκοσαετοῦς), [[matthew 2 16|Mat.2:16.]]† (AS)
διετία, -ας, ἡ (διετής), [in LXX (Græc. Ven.): [[genesis 41 1|Gen.41:1 45:5]] * ;] the space of two years: [[acts 24 27|Act.24:27 28:30]].† (AS)

δι-ηγέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX chiefly for סָפַר pi. ;] to set out in detail, recount, describe: absol., [[hebrews 11 32|Heb.11:32;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[acts 8 33|Act.8:33;]] with dative of person(s), before πῶς, [[mark 5 16|Mrk.5:16]], [[acts 9 27|Act.9:27 12:17]]; ἅ εἶδον, [[mark 9 9|Mrk.9:9;]] ὅσα ἐποίησε, -αν, [[luke 8 39|Luk.8:39 9:10]].† (AS)

δι-ήγησις, -εως, ἡ (διηγέομαι), [in LXX: [[judges 7 15|Jdg.7:15]] מִסְפָּר [[habakkuk 2 6|Hab.2:6]] חִידָה), frequently in (Sir.6:35, al.), 2Ma.2:32 2Mac 6:17 ;] a narrative: [[luke 1 1|Luk.1:1]] (cf. Milligan, NTD, 130).† (AS)

δι-ηνεκής, -ές (διήνεγκα, aorist of διαφέρω) [in Sm.: [[psalms 48 15|Psa.48:15, 89:30]] ;] unbroken, continuous: adverbially, εἰς τὸ δ., continually (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 251), [[hebrews 7 3|Heb.7:3 10:1, 12 10:14]]† (AS)

διθάλασσος, -ον (δις, θύλασσα); 1. divided into two seas (as the Euxine, Strab., ii, 522). 2. dividing the sea: τόπον δ., a tongue of land, or reef, running out into the sea: [[acts 27 41|Act.27:41.]]† (AS)
δι-ικνέομαι (Rec. διϊκ-), -οῦμαι, [in LXX for בָּרַח hi., [[exodus 26 28|Exo.26:28]] * ;] to go through, penetrate: [[hebrews 4 12|Heb.4:12.]]† (AS)

δι-ίσπημι (Rec. διΐσ), [in LXX: [[ezekiel 5 1|Eze.5:1]] (חָלַק pi.), [[proverbs 17 9|Pro.17:9]] (פָּרַד hi.), etc. ;] to set apart, separate; of time (or space), to make an interval, intervene: διαστάσης ὥρας μιᾶς, [[luke 22 59|Luk.22:59;]] βραχὺ διαστήσαντες, [[acts 27 28|Act.27:28.]] In pass., mid. and 2 aor., pf. and plpf. act., to part, withdraw: [[luke 24 51|Luk.24:51.]]† (AS)
δι-ισχυρίζομαι (T, Rec. διϊσ-), depon.; 1. to lean upon. 2. to affirm confidently: with ptcp., [[luke 22 59|Luk.22:59;]] with accusative and inf. (Bl., § 70, 3), [[acts 12 15|Act.12:15.]]† (AS)

δικαιοκρισία, -ας, ἡ righteous judgment: [[romans 2 5|Rom.2:5]] (cf. τ. δικαίας κρίσεως, [[2-thessalonians 1 5|2Th.1:5;]] τὴν δ. κ., [[john 7 24|Jhn.7:24.]] For use in π., see Deiss., LAE, 89 f.).† (AS)

δίκαιος, -α, -ον (δίκη), [in LXX chiefly for צַדִּיק (for rendering of צַדִּיק in sense of correct, see Deiss., BS, 115 f.); sometimes for נָקִי as [[proverbs 1 11|Pro.1:11]], al. ;] in early Gk. writers (a) of persons, observant of δίκη, custom, rule, right, righteous in performing duties to gods and men ; (b) of things, righteous, in accordance with right. In NT 1. righteous, chiefly in the broad sense, as above, of the person or thing corresponding to the Divine standard of right (a) of persons: of God, [[romans 3 26|Rom.3:26]], [[1-john 2 29|1Jn.2:29]] [[john 3 7|Jn 3:7]]; of Christ, [[acts 3 14|Act.3:14 7:52 22:14]], [[1-peter 3 18|1Pe.3:18]], [[1-john 2 1|1Jn.2:1]]; of men, [[matthew 1 19|Mat.1:19]] (Abbott, Essays, 75 f.) [[matthew 10 41|Mat.10:41 13:17, 43 13:49]], [[luke 1 6|Luk.1:6, 17]], [[romans 5 7|Rom.5:7]], [[1-timothy 1 9|1Ti.1:9]], [[james 5 6|Jas.5:6]], [[1-peter 3 12|1Pe.3:12]], [[1-john 3 7|1Jn.3:7]], [[revelation 22 11|Rev.22:11]], al.; δ. καὶ εὐλαβής, [[luke 2 25|Luk.2:25;]] ἅγιος, [[mark 6 20|Mrk.6:20;]] ἀγαθός, [[luke 23 50|Luk.23:50;]] φοβούμενος τ. θεόν, [[acts 10 22|Act.10:22;]] opposite to ἀμαρτωλοὶ καὶ ἀσεβεῖς, [[1-peter 4 18|1Pe.4:18;]] ἄδικοι, [[matthew 5 45|Mat.5:45]], [[acts 24 15|Act.24:15]]; δ. ἐκ πίστεως, [[romans 1 17|Rom.1:17]], [[galatians 3 11|Gal.3:11]], [[hebrews 10 38|Heb.10:38]]" (LXX) ; δ. παρὰ τ. θεῷ, [[romans 2 13|Rom.2:13]] (b) of things: ἔργα δ., opposite to πονηρὰ, [[1-john 3 12|1Jn.3:12;]] ἐντολή, [[romans 7 12|Rom.7:12;]] metaphorically, αἷμα, [[matthew 23 35|Mat.23:35;]] τὸ δ., [[luke 12 57|Luk.12:57;]] δ. ἐστιν, [[acts 4 19|Act.4:19]], [[ephesians 6 1|Eph.6:1]], [[philippians 1 7|Php.1:7]]; ὅ, [[matthew 20 4|Mat.20:4;]] ὅσα, [[philippians 4 8|Php.4:8]] 2. In narrower sense (a) of persons, as in later cl. writers, just, rendering to each his due: [[titus 1 8|Tit.1:8]], [[1-john 1 9|1Jn.1:9]]; δ. κριτής, [[2-timothy 4 8|2Ti.4:8]] (b) of things: τὸ δ., [[colossians 4 1|Col.4:1;]] δ., sc. ἐστιν, [[2-thessalonians 1 6|2Th.1:6;]] κρίσις δ., [[john 5 30|Jhn.5:30;]] ὁδοί, [[revelation 15 3|Rev.15:3]] SYN.: ἀγαθός (which see), καλός, χρηστός (Cremer, 183, 690). (AS)

δικαιοσύνη, -ης, ἡ (δίκαιος), [in LXX chiefly for צֶדֶק, and cognates, [[genesis 15 6|Gen.15:6]], al., rarely for חֶסֶד, [[genesis 19 19|Gen.19:19]] ;] the character of ὁ δίκαιος (which see) 1. in broad sense, righteousness, conformity to the Divine will in purpose, thought and action: [[matthew 5 6|Mat.5:6]], [[john 16 8|Jhn.16:8]], [[acts 13 10|Act.13:10]], [[romans 4 3|Rom.4:3]]; λόγος δικαιοσύνης, teaching of r., [[hebrews 5 13|Heb.5:13;]] βασιλεὺς δ. (cf. FlJ, BJ, vi, 10, β. δίκαιος), [[hebrews 7 2|Heb.7:2;]] ὅπλα δ., [[romans 6 13|Rom.6:13;]] ὁδὸς δ., [[matthew 21 32|Mat.21:32;]] θώραξ τῆς δ., [[ephesians 6 14|Eph.6:14;]] διὰκονοι δ., [[2-corinthians 11 15|2Co.11:15;]] ὁσιότης καὶ δ., [[luke 1 75|Luk.1:75]], cf. [[ephesians 4 24|Eph.4:24;]] ἀγαθωσύνῃ καὶ δ., [[ephesians 5 9|Eph.5:9;]] δ. κ. εἰρήνη κ. χαρά, [[romans 14 17|Rom.14:17;]] δ. κ. ἁγιασμός, [[1-corinthians 1 30|1Co.1:30;]] opposite to ἁμαρτία, [[romans 8 10|Rom.8:10;]] ἀνομία, [[2-corinthians 6 14|2Co.6:14;]] άδικία, [[romans 3 5|Rom.3:5;]] ποιεῖν τὴν δ., [[1-john 2 29|1Jn.2:29]] [[john 3 7|Jn 3:7]]; id. as an inclusive term for the active duties of the religious life (ICC, in l; Abbott, Essays, 73 ff), [[matthew 6 1|Mat.6:1;]] ἐργάζεσθαι δ., [[acts 10 35|Act.10:35;]] διώκειν δ., [[1-timothy 6 11|1Ti.6:11;]] πληροῦν πᾶσαν δ., [[matthew 3 15|Mat.3:15;]] ζῆν τῇ δ., [[1-peter 2 24|1Pe.2:24;]] δ. θεοῦ, a righteousness divine in its character and origin, [[matthew 6 33|Mat.6:33]], [[james 1 20|Jas.1:20]], (where it also includes the idea of God's personal r.; see ICC, on [[romans 1 17|Rom.1:17]]) [[romans 1 17|Rom.1:17 3:5, 21-26 10:3]], [[2-corinthians 5 21|2Co.5:21]], [[philippians 3 9|Php.3:9]]; ἡ δ. τ. πίσιεως, [[romans 4 11|Rom.4:11;]] ἡ ἐκ π. δ., [[romans 9 30|Rom.9:30;]] ἡ κατὰ π. δ., [[hebrews 11 7|Heb.11:7;]] opposite to this is ἡ ἐκ νόμου δ., [[romans 10 5|Rom.10:5;]] ἡ δ. ἐν ν., [[philippians 3 6|Php.3:6;]] ἡ ἰδία δ., [[romans 10 3|Rom.10:3]], cf. δικαιόω, -ῶ (δίκαιος), [in LXX chiefly for צָדַק pi., hi., (1) as [[ezekiel 16 51|Eze.16:51]], [[jeremiah 3 11|Jer.3:11]] (cf. NT usage); (2) as [[deuteronomy 25 1|Deu.25:1;]] [[exodus 23 7|Exo.23:7]], [[isaiah 50 8|Isa.50:8]] ;] 1. in cl., (a) with accusative of thing(s), to deem right; (b) with accusative of person(s), to do one justice; pass., δικαιοῦσθαι, to be treated rightly, opposite to ἀδικεῖσθαι. 2. In NT, as in LXX, and as usual with verbs in -όω from adjectives of moral meaning; (1) to show to be righteous: [[matthew 11 19|Mat.11:19]], [[luke 7 35|Luk.7:35]], [[romans 3 4|Rom.3:4]]" (LXX), [[1-timothy 3 16|1Ti.3:16;]] (2) to declare, pronounce righteous: [[luke 7 29|Luk.7:29 10:29 16:15 18:14]], [[romans 2 13|Rom.2:13 3:24, 26 3:28 4:5 8:30, 33]], [[titus 3 7|Tit.3:7]]; before ἀπό, [[matthew 11 19|Mat.11:19]], [[luke 7 35|Luk.7:35]], [[acts 13 39|Act.13:39]], [[romans 6 7|Rom.6:7]]; ἐκ πίστεως, [[romans 3 30|Rom.3:30 5:1]], [[galatians 2 16|Gal.2:16 3:8, 24]]; ἐξ ἔργων, [[romans 3 20|Rom.3:20]] (LXX) [[romans 4 2|Rom.4:2]], [[galatians 2 16|Gal.2:16]], [[james 2 21|Jas.2:21, 24-25]]; ἐκ τ. λόγων, [[matthew 12 37|Mat.12:37;]] διὰ τ. πίστεως, [[romans 3 30|Rom.3:30;]] with dative, [[romans 3 24|Rom.3:24, 28]], [[titus 3 7|Tit.3:7]]; before ἐν, [[acts 13 39|Act.13:39]], [[romans 3 4|Rom.3:4 5:9]], [[1-corinthians 4 4|1Co.4:4 6:11]], [[galatians 2 17|Gal.2:17 3:11 5:4]], [[1-timothy 3 16|1Ti.3:16]] (see Cremer, 193, 693; DB, ii, 826 ff.).† (AS)

δικαίωμα, -τος, τ (δικαιόω), [in LXX most frequently for חֹק, in Ez, chiefly for מִשְׁפָּט, in Pss, τὰ δ., frequently for פִּקּוּד ;] a concrete expression of righteousness, the expression and result of the act of δικαίωσις, "a declaration that a thing is δίκαιον, or that a person is δίκαιος," hence, (a) an ordinance: δ. τ. θεοῦ, [[romans 1 32|Rom.1:32;]] τ. κυρίου, [[luke 1 6|Luk.1:6;]] τ. νόμου, [[romans 2 26|Rom.2:26 8:4]]; λατρείας, [[hebrews 9 1|Heb.9:1;]] σαρκός, [[hebrews 9 10|Heb.9:10;]] (b) a sentence: of acquittal, [[romans 5 16|Rom.5:16]] (also [[romans 5 18|Rom.5:18;]] ICC, in l), or of condemnation; (with) a righteous act: [[romans 5 18|Rom.5:18]] (RV), [[revelation 15 4|Rev.15:4 19:8]] (on the usage of π., see MM, Exp., iii, xi). † (AS)

δικαίως adv. (δίκαιος, which see), [in LXX for צֶדֶק, etc. ;] 1. righteously: [[1-corinthians 15 34|1Co.15:34]], [[1-thessalonians 2 10|1Th.2:10]], [[titus 2 12|Tit.2:12]]. 2. justly: [[luke 23 41|Luk.23:41]], [[1-peter 2 23|1Pe.2:23]].† (AS)
δικαίωσις, -εως, ἡ (δικαιόω), [in LXX for מִשְׁפָּט, [[leviticus 24 22|Lev.24:22]] * ;] the act of pronouncing righteous, justification, acquittal: [[romans 4 25|Rom.4:25 5:18]] (Cremer, 199).† (AS)

δικαστής, -οῦ, ὁ (δικάζω), [in LXX for שָׁפַט ;] a judge: [[acts 7 27|Act.7:27, 35]]" (LXX) .† SYN.: κριτής, WH. "gives prominence to the mental process" (Thayer). δ. is the forensic term. In Attic law, the δικασταί were jurors, with a κριτής as presiding officer (LS, see word; Enc. Brit. 11, xii, 504 f.) (AS)

δίκη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX for נָקָם, רִיב, etc. ;] 1. custom. 2. right. 3. a judicial hearing; hence its result, the execution of a sentence, punishment: δ. τίνειν, [[2-thessalonians 1 9|2Th.1:9;]] δ. υπεχειν, Ju 7. 4. Personified (cf. Lat. Justitia), justice, vengeance: [[acts 28 4|Act.28:4.]]† (AS)

δίκτυον, -ον, τό [in LXX chiefly for רֶשֶׁת, שְׂבָכָה ;] general term for a net: [[matthew 4 20|Mat.4:20-21]], [[mark 1 18|Mrk.1:18-19]], [[luke 5 2|Luk.5:2, 4-6]], [[john 21 6|Jhn.21:6, 8 21:11]] † SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (which see), σαγήνη. (AS)

διλογος, -ον (δίς, λέγω), 1. in sense of διλογεῖν, -ία (Xen.), given to repetition. 2. In NT, prob. (cf. δίγλωσσος, [[proverbs 11 13|Pro.11:13]], Sir.5:9) double-tongued: [[1-timothy 3 8|1Ti.3:8.]]† (AS)

διό conjunct. for δι᾽ ὅ, wherefore, on which account: [[matthew 27 8|Mat.27:8]], [[luke 7 7|Luk.7:7]], [[acts 15 19|Act.15:19]], [[romans 1 24|Rom.1:24]], al.; δ. καί, [[luke 1 35|Luk.1:35]], [[acts 10 29|Act.10:29 24:26]], [[romans 4 22|Rom.4:22 15:22]], [[2-corinthians 1 20|2Co.1:20 4:13 5:9]], [[philippians 2 9|Php.2:9]], [[hebrews 11 12|Heb.11:12 13:12]] (see Ellic. on [[galatians 4 31|Gal.4:31]]). (AS)
δι-οδεύω, [in LXX chiefly for עבר ;] 1. to travel through: with accusative, [[acts 17 1|Act.17:1]] 2. to travel along (Bar.4:2, 1Ma.12:32-33): [[luke 8 1|Luk.8:1]].† (AS)
Διονύσιος, -ου, ὁ Dionysius, an Athenian: [[acts 17 34|Act.17:34.]]† (AS)
διό-περ conjunct. (διό, which see, strengthened by πέρ), [in LXX: Jdth.8:17; Jdt.8.1-36; 2Ma.5:1-27 * ;] for which very reason: [[1-corinthians 8 13|1Co.8:13 10:14]].† (AS)

διοπετής (written also διϊπ-), -ές (δῖος, πίπτω, see Page on Ac, l.with; DB, i, 605, n., ext., 112a; Field, Notes, 130 f.), fallen from heaven (R, mg.): τὸ δ. (sc. ἄγαλμα, statue, image), [[acts 19 35|Act.19:35.]]† (AS)

διόρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (see supr.), 1. a making straight. 2. a reforming, reformation (used in late writers of laws, etc.): [[hebrews 9 10|Heb.9:10]] (Cremer, 807).† διόρθωμα, -τος, τό (διορθόω, to make straight, set right), a correction, reform: [[acts 24 3|Act.24:3.]]† διόρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (see supr.), 1. a making straight. 2. a reforming, reformation (used in late writers of laws, etc.): [[hebrews 9 10|Heb.9:10]] (Cremer, 807).† (AS)

δι-ορύσσω [in LXX: [[job 24 16|Job.24:16]], [[exodus 12 5|Exo.12:5, 7 12:12]], (חָתַר) * ;] to dig through: with accusative, of house-breaking (as in π.; MM, Exp., xi), [[matthew 24 43|Mat.24:43]], [[luke 12 39|Luk.12:39]]; absol., [[matthew 6 19|Mat.6:19-20.]]† (AS)

Διόσ-κουροι, -ων, οἱ (Ion. and κοινή form of Att..., Διόσκοροι; Διός, genitive of Ζεύς + κόρος, a son), the Dioscuri (Castor and Pollux), twin sons of Zeus and Leda (RV, The Twin Brothers): [[acts 28 11|Act.28:11.]]† (AS)

δι-ότι , conjunct., for διὰ τοῦτο, ὅτι (Lat. propterea quod), because: [[luke 1 13|Luk.1:13 2:7 21:28]], [[acts 13 35|Act.13:35 18:10 20:26 22:18]], [[romans 1 19|Rom.1:19, 21 3:20 8:7, 21]], [[1-corinthians 15 9|1Co.15:9]], [[philippians 2 26|Php.2:26]], [[1-thessalonians 2 8|1Th.2:8, 18]] (Lft., Notes, 37) [[1-thessalonians 4 6|1Th.4:6]], [[hebrews 11 5|Heb.11:5, 23]], [[james 4 3|Jas.4:3]], [[1-peter 1 16|1Pe.1:16 1:24 2:6]]. It is usually stronger than ὅτι, but sometimes, as in [[luke 1 13|Luk.1:13]], [[romans 1 19|Rom.1:19]], [[1-thessalonians 2 18|1Th.2:18]], approximates to MGr. sense, for; cf. Milligan, Th., l.with† (AS)
Διοτρέφης (Rec. -τρεψής), -ες (Διός, genitive of Ζεύς + τρέφω: cherished by Zeus), as proper name, Diotrephes: III Jn 9.† (AS)

διπλόος (poët., διπλός, whence corp. -ότερον), -όη, -όον (-οῦ, -ῆ, -οῦν) [in LXX for כָּפַל, מִשְׁנֶה, and cognates ;] twofold, double: [[1-timothy 5 17|1Ti.5:17]], [[revelation 18 6|Rev.18:6]]; διπλότιρον, in twofold measure: [[matthew 23 15|Mat.23:15.]]† (AS)
διπλόω, -ῶ (δυτλόος), to double: δ. τὰ διπλᾶ, [[revelation 18 6|Rev.18:6.]]† (AS)

δίς adv., twice: [[mark 14 30|Mrk.14:30, 72]]; δ. τ. σαββάτου, [[luke 18 12|Luk.18:12;]] καὶ ἅπαξ κ. δ., [[philippians 4 16|Php.4:16]], [[1-thessalonians 2 18|1Th.2:18]]; δ. ἀποθανόντα, Ju 12 (see Mayor, ICC, in l); δ. μυριάδες, [[revelation 9 16|Rev.9:16.]]† (AS)
διστάζω (δίς), to doubt, hesitate: [[matthew 14 31|Mat.14:31 28:17]].† SYN.: ἀπορέω, διαπορέω, διακρίνομαι, μετεωρίζομαι (see DCG, i, 491) (AS)

δίστομος, -ον (δίς, στόμα), [in LXX: [[judges 3 16|Jdg.3:16]], [[psalms 149 6|Psa.149:6]], [[proverbs 5 4|Pro.5:4]] (פֶּה), Sir.21:3 * ;] 1. of rivers and roads, double-mouthed, double branching. 2. Of swords (Eur.; LXX, ll with), two-edged: [[hebrews 4 12|Heb.4:12]], [[revelation 1 16|Rev.1:16 2:12]].† (AS)
two thousand , (Herdotus Historicus):—;singular with collective nouns, δισχιλίη ἵππος 2000 horse, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)
δι-υλίζω (δια, ὑλίζω, to strain) [in LXX: [[amos 6 6|Amo.6:6]] * ;] 1. to strain thoroughly (Archytas; Am., l.with). 2. Later, to strain out: figuratively, [[matthew 23 24|Mat.23:24.]]† (AS)
διχάζω (δίχα, apart), [in Aq.: [[leviticus 1 17|Lev.1:17]], [[deuteronomy 14 6|Deu.14:6]] * ;] to cut apart, divide in two; metaphorically, to set at variance: [[matthew 10 35|Mat.10:35.]]† (AS)
διχοστασία, -ας, ἡ (διχοστατέω, to stand apart), [in LXX: 1Ma.3:29 * ;] standing apart, dissension: [[romans 16 17|Rom.16:17]], [[galatians 5 20|Gal.5:20]].† (AS)

διχοτομέω, -ῶ (διχοτόμος, δίχα, τέμνω), [in LXX: [[exodus 29 17|Exo.29:17]] (נָתַח pi.) ;] to cut in two, cut asunder: perh. metaphorically of severe scourging (but see Meyer on Mt, l.with, and cf. [[1-kings 15 33|1Ki.15:33]], [[2-samuel 12 31|2Ki.12:31]], [[hebrews 11 37|Heb.11:37]]), [[matthew 24 51|Mat.24:51]], [[luke 12 46|Luk.12:46]].† (AS)

διψάω,-ῶ (δίψα, thirst), [in LXX chiefly for צָמֵא ;] to thirst: absol., [[matthew 25 35|Mat.25:35, 37 25:42, 44]], [[john 4 13|Jhn.4:13, 15 19:28]], [[romans 12 20|Rom.12:20]]" (LXX), [[1-corinthians 4 11|1Co.4:11;]] figuratively, [[john 4 14|Jhn.4:14 6:35 7:37]], [[revelation 7 16|Rev.7:16 21:6 22:17]]; with accusative (= cl. with genitive), τ. δικαιοσύνην, [[matthew 5 6|Mat.5:6.]]† (AS)
δίψος, -εος (-ους), τό (late form of δίψα), [in LXX chiefly for and cognates ;] thirst: [[2-corinthians 11 27|2Co.11:27.]]† (AS)
δίψυχος, -ον (δίς, ψυχή), of two minds, wavering: [[james 1 8|Jas.1:8 4:8]] (Cremer, 588; DB, iv, 528).† (AS)

διωγμός, -oῦ, ὁ (διώκω), [in LXX: [[proverbs 11 19|Pro.11:19]] (רָדַף pi.), [[lamentations 3 19|La 3:19]] (מָרוּד), 2Ma.12:23 * ;] persecution: [[matthew 13 21|Mat.13:21]], [[mark 4 17|Mrk.4:17 10:30]] [[acts 8 1|Act.8:1 13:50]], [[romans 8 35|Rom.8:35]], [[2-corinthians 12 10|2Co.12:10]], [[2-thessalonians 1 4|2Th.1:4]], [[2-timothy 3 11|2Ti.3:11]].† (AS)
διώκτης, -ου, ὁ (διώκω), a persecutor: [[1-timothy 1 13|1Ti.1:13.]]† (AS)

διώκω [in LXX chiefly for רָדַף ;] 1. to put to flight, drive away: [[matthew 23 34|Mat.23:34.]] 2. to pursue; (a) of persons; with accusative, without hostility, to follow after: [[luke 17 23|Luk.17:23;]] with hostile purpose: [[acts 26 11|Act.26:11]], [[revelation 12 13|Rev.12:13]]. δόγμα, -τος, τό (δοκέω), [in LXX chiefly for דָּת, טְעֵם ;] 1. an opinion. 2. A public decree, ordinance: of Roman rulers, [[luke 2 1|Luk.2:1]], [[acts 17 7|Act.17:7]]; of the Jewish law, [[ephesians 2 15|Eph.2:15]], [[colossians 2 14|Col.2:14]]; of the Apostles, [[acts 16 4|Act.16:4]] (Cremer, 205).† (AS)

δογματίζω [in LXX: [[esther 3 9|Est.3:9]] (כָּתַב ni.), Dan LXX 2:13, 15 (דָּת), I [[esther 6 34|Est.6:34]], 2Ma.10:3 2Mac 15:36, 3Ma.4:11 * ;] to decree. Mid., to subject oneself to an ordinance: [[colossians 2 20|Col.2:20.]]† (AS)

δοκέω, -ῶ (δόκος, opinion, δέκομαι, Ion, form of δέχ-), [in LXX for טוֹב, נָדַב, etc. ;] 1. to be of opinion, suppose: [[matthew 24 44|Mat.24:44]], [[luke 12 40|Luk.12:40]], [[hebrews 10 29|Heb.10:29]]; with inf., [[matthew 3 9|Mat.3:9]], [[luke 8 18|Luk.8:18 24:37]], [[john 5 39|Jhn.5:39 16:2]], [[acts 12 9|Act.12:9 27:13]], [[1-corinthians 3 18|1Co.3:18 7:40 8:2 10:12 14:37]], [[galatians 6 3|Gal.6:3]], [[philippians 3 4|Php.3:4]], [[james 1 26|Jas.1:26]]; with accusative and inf., [[1-corinthians 12 23|1Co.12:23]], [[2-corinthians 11 16|2Co.11:16]]; before ὅτι, [[matthew 6 7|Mat.6:7 26:53]], [[mark 6 49|Mrk.6:49]], [[luke 12 51|Luk.12:51 13:2, 4 19:11]], [[john 5 45|Jhn.5:45 11:13, 31 13:29 20:15]], [[1-corinthians 4 9|1Co.4:9]], [[2-corinthians 12 19|2Co.12:19]], [[james 4 5|Jas.4:5]]. 2. to seem, be reputed: [[acts 25 27|Act.25:27;]] with inf., [[mark 10 42|Mrk.10:42]], [[luke 10 36|Luk.10:36 22:24]], [[acts 17 13|Act.17:13 26:9]], [[1-corinthians 11 16|1Co.11:16 12:22]], [[2-corinthians 10 9|2Co.10:9]], [[galatians 2 6|Gal.2:6]], 9, [[hebrews 4 1|Heb.4:1 12:11]]; οἱ δοκοῦντες, those of repute, [[galatians 2 2|Gal.2:2.]] Impers., it seems, with dative of person(s); (a) to think: [[matthew 17 25|Mat.17:25 18:12 21:28 22:17, 42 26:66]], [[john 11 56|Jhn.11:56]], [[hebrews 12 10|Heb.12:10]]; (b) to please, seem good to: with inf., [[luke 1 3|Luk.1:3]], [[acts 15 22|Act.15:22, 25 15:23, 34]].† SYN. (δοκέω 1): ἡγέομαι 2, νομίζω2, οἴομαι; ἡ. and ν. properly express belief resting on external proof, ἡ. denoting the more careful judgment; δ. and οἴ. imply a subjective judgment which in the case of οἴ. is based on feeling, in δ. on thought (see Schmidt, with 17) (δοκέω2): φαίνομαι; φ., from the standpoint of the object, "expresses how a matter phenomenally shows and presents itself"; δ., from the standpoint of the observer, expresses one's subjective judgment about a matter (see Tr., Syn., LXXx; Cremer, 204). (AS)

δοκιμάζω (δόκιμος), [in LXX chiefly for בָּחַן ;] 1. primarily of metals ([[proverbs 8 10|Pro.8:10 17:3]], Sir.2:5, Wis.3:6), to test, try, prove (in the hope and expectation that the test will prove successful, see reff. s. Syn.): χρυσίον, [[1-peter 1 7|1Pe.1:7;]] other things, [[luke 12 56|Luk.12:56 14:19]], [[2-corinthians 8 8|2Co.8:8]], [[galatians 6 4|Gal.6:4]], [[1-thessalonians 2 4|1Th.2:4 5:21]]; τὰ διαφέροντα, [[romans 2 18|Rom.2:18]], [[philippians 1 10|Php.1:10]] (R, mg., but see infr.); πνεύματα, [[1-john 4 1|1Jn.4:1;]] of men, [[1-timothy 3 10|1Ti.3:10]] (pass.); ἑαυτόν, [[1-corinthians 11 28|1Co.11:28]], [[2-corinthians 13 5|2Co.13:5]]; before subst. clause, [[romans 12 2|Rom.12:2]], [[1-corinthians 3 13|1Co.3:13]], [[ephesians 5 10|Eph.5:10]] 2. As the result of trial, to approve, think fit: [[romans 1 28|Rom.1:28 14:22]], [[1-corinthians 16 3|1Co.16:3]], [[2-corinthians 8 22|2Co.8:22]], [[1-thessalonians 2 4|1Th.2:4]] (δεδοκιμάσμεθα); τὰ διαφέροντα, [[romans 2 18|Rom.2:18]], [[philippians 1 10|Php.1:10]], R, txt. (but see supr.; cf. διαφέρω).† (AS)

δοκιμή, -ῆς, ἡ (δόκιμος), [in Sm.: [[psalms 68 31|Psa.68:31]] * ;] 1. the process of trial, proving, test: [[2-corinthians 8 2|2Co.8:2 9:13]] 2. The result of trial, approval, approvedness, proof: [[romans 5 4|Rom.5:4]], [[2-corinthians 2 9|2Co.2:9 13:3]], [[philippians 2 22|Php.2:22]] (Cremer, 212, 701).† (AS)

δοκίμιον, -ου, τό [in LXX: [[proverbs 17 3|Pro.17:3 27:21]] (מִצְרֵף) * ;] usually regarded as a variant form of δοκιμεῖον, a test, and so perh. [[james 1 3|Jas.1:3]] (see Mayor, in l), but see next word (cf. Cremer, 212, 702).† (AS)

δοκίμιος, -α, -ον (δοκιμή), [in LXX: ἀργύριον δ. (עֲלִיל), [[psalms 12 6|Psa.12:6;]] and as seel. for δόκιμος (B), ἀργυρίου δ. (זָקַק pual.), [[1-chronicles 29 4|1Ch.29:4]] (Bab); εἰ δ .ίστιν (יְקָר), [[zechariah 11 13|Zec.11:13]] א with a vid, Q *)* ;] = δόκιμος, tested, approved: τὸ δ. ὑμῶν τ. πίστεως, that which is approved in your faith, [[1-peter 1 7|1Pe.1:7]] (where Hort suggests the seel. δόκιμος, found in some cursives), [[james 1 3|Jas.1:3]] (but see Mayor, in l For full discussion of this word, not hitherto found in a Gk. Lexicon, and for exx. of its use in π., see Deiss. (to whom is due the credit of its discovery), BS, 259 ff.; MM, Exp., xi; cf. also Milligan, NTD, 76).† δόκιμος, -ον (δέκομαι = δέχομαι) [in LXX for זָקַק pual., etc. ;] primarily of metals, tested, accepted, approved: of persons, [[romans 14 18|Rom.14:18 16:10]], [[1-corinthians 11 19|1Co.11:19]], [[2-corinthians 10 18|2Co.10:18 13:7]], [[2-timothy 2 15|2Ti.2:15]], [[james 1 12|Jas.1:12]] (Cremer, 212, 697).† (AS)
δοκός, -οῦ, ἡ (δέχομαι) [in LXX for קוֹרָה, etc. ;] a beam of timber: [[matthew 7 3|Mat.7:3-5]], [[luke 6 41|Luk.6:41-42]] (DCG, i, 176).† (AS)
δόλιος, -α, -ον (δόλος), [in LXX—chiefly in Pss, Pr, Sir—for etc. ;] deceitful: [[2-corinthians 11 13|2Co.11:13.]]† (AS)

δολιόω (δόλιος), [in LXX: [[numbers 25 18|Num.25:18]], [[psalms 105 25|Psa.105:25]] (נָכַל), [[psalms 5 6|Psa.5:6]] (חָלַק hi.) * ;] to deceive: ἐδολιοῦσαν (-σαν, frequently in κοινή Gk. for imperfect 3rd of person(s) pl.), [[romans 3 13|Rom.3:13]] (LXX).† (AS)

δόλος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for מִרְמָה;] 1. in Hom., a bait. 2. a snare. 3. In the abstract, craft, deceit: [[matthew 26 4|Mat.26:4]], [[mark 7 22|Mrk.7:22 14:1]], [[john 1 47|Jhn.1:47]], [[acts 13 10|Act.13:10]], [[romans 1 29|Rom.1:29]], [[2-corinthians 12 16|2Co.12:16]], [[1-thessalonians 2 3|1Th.2:3]], [[1-peter 2 1|1Pe.2:1 2:22 3:10]]" (LXX) (λαλῆσαι δ.).† (AS)

δόμα, -τος, τό (δίδωμι), [in LXX for מַתָּנָה, etc. ;] a gift: [[matthew 7 11|Mat.7:11]], [[luke 11 13|Luk.11:13]], [[ephesians 4 8|Eph.4:8]]" (LXX), [[philippians 4 17|Php.4:17.]]† SYN.: δόσις, δῶρον, δωρεά, δώρημα (AS)

δόξα, -ης, ἡ (δοκέω), [in LXX very frequently for כָּבוֹד, also for הוֹד ,פִּפְאֶרֶת, etc., 25 words in all ;] in cl., 1. expectation, judgment, opinion (4Ma.5:18). 2. opinion, estimation in which one is held, repute; in NT, always good opinion, hence reputation, praise, honour, glory: [[luke 14 10|Luk.14:10]], [[john 12 43|Jhn.12:43]], [[hebrews 3 3|Heb.3:3]]; opposite to αἰσχύνη, [[philippians 3 19|Php.3:19;]] to ἀτιμία, [[2-corinthians 6 8|2Co.6:8;]] δ. κ. τιμή, [[romans 2 7|Rom.2:7, 10]] [[1-peter 1 7|1Pe.1:7]], [[2-peter 1 17|2Pe.1:17]]; ζητεῖν, [[john 5 44|Jhn.5:44 7:18 8:50]], [[1-thessalonians 2 6|1Th.2:6]]; λαμβάνειν, [[john 5 41|Jhn.5:41]], [[2-peter 1 17|2Pe.1:17]], [[revelation 5 12|Rev.5:12]]; διδόναι δ. τ. θεῷ (cf. נָתַן כָּבוֹד לַיהוָֹה, [[jeremiah 13 16|Jer.13:16]], al.), [[luke 17 18|Luk.17:18]], [[john 9 24|Jhn.9:24]], [[acts 12 23|Act.12:23]], [[romans 4 20|Rom.4:20]], [[revelation 4 9|Rev.4:9]]; εἰς (τ.) δ. θεοῦ, [[romans 3 7|Rom.3:7 15:7]], [[philippians 1 11|Php.1:11]], al.; in doxologies, τ. θεῷ (ᾧ) ἡ δ., [[luke 2 14|Luk.2:14]], [[romans 11 36|Rom.11:36 16:27]], [[galatians 1 5|Gal.1:5]], [[ephesians 3 21|Eph.3:21]], al. 3. Later also (not cl.) as in LXX (= הוֹד, [[job 39 20|Job.39:20]], [[1-chronicles 29 25|1Ch.29:25]]; כָּבוֹד, [[job 19 9|Job.19:9]], [[esther 5 11|Est.5:11]], al.), visible brightness, splendour, glory: of light, [[acts 22 11|Act.22:11;]] of heavenly bodies, [[1-corinthians 15 40|1Co.15:40]]ff.; esp. that wh. radiates from God's presence, as manifested in the pillar of cloud and in the Holy of Holies (= כָּבוֹד, [[exodus 16 10|Exo.16:10 25:22 40:34]], al.; and new Heb. שְׁכִינָה, 2Ma.2:8; see DB, iv, 489b), [[romans 9 4|Rom.9:4]], [[james 2 1|Jas.2:1]] (see Hort, Mayor, in l.); hence of the manifested glory of God, [[romans 1 23|Rom.1:23]], [[colossians 1 11|Col.1:11]] [[ephesians 1 6|Eph.1:6, 12 17 3:16]]; of the same as communicated to man through Christ, [[2-corinthians 3 18|2Co.3:18 4:6]]; and of the glorious condition into which Christians shall enter hereafter, [[romans 8 18|Rom.8:18, 21 9:23]], [[2-timothy 2 10|2Ti.2:10]], al. SYN.: ἔπαινος τιμή (see Hort on [[1-peter 1 7|1Pe.1:7]]). (AS)

δοξάζω (δόξα), [in LXX chiefly for כָּבַד ni., pi., also for פָּאַר, etc. ;] 1. to think, suppose, hold an opinion (Æsch., Plat., al.). 2. To bestow δόξα (which see) on, to magnify, extol, praise (Thuc., iii, 45; Plut., al.): with accusative, [[matthew 5 16|Mat.5:16]], [[mark 2 12|Mrk.2:12]], [[john 8 54|Jhn.8:54]], [[romans 15 6|Rom.15:6]], [[1-peter 2 12|1Pe.2:12]], al.; id. before ἐπί [[luke 2 20|Luk.2:20;]] ἐν, [[galatians 1 24|Gal.1:24]], [[1-peter 4 16|1Pe.4:16]]. 3. In LXX and NT (see: δόξα, 3), to clothe with splendour, glorify ([[exodus 34 29|Exo.34:29-30]], [[psalms 37 20|Psa.37:20]], [[isaiah 44 23|Isa.44:23]], [[esther 3 1|Est.3:1]], al): [[romans 8 30|Rom.8:30]], [[2-corinthians 3 10|2Co.3:10]], [[2-thessalonians 3 1|2Th.3:1]], [[1-peter 1 8|1Pe.1:8]], al.; of Christ, [[john 7 39|Jhn.7:39 8:54]], al. (on the Johannine use, see Cremer, 211; Westc., Jo., Intr.); of the Father, [[john 13 31|Jhn.13:31-32]], [[1-peter 4 11|1Pe.4:11]], al. (cf. ἐν-, συν-δοξάζω). (AS)
Δορκάς, -άδος, ἡ (δορκάς, a gazelle), Dorcas, also called Ταβειθά, which see: [[acts 9 36|Act.9:36, 39]].† (AS)

δόσις, -εως, ἡ (δίδωμι) [in LXX for חֹק ([[genesis 47 22|Gen.47:22]]), ([[proverbs 21 14|Pro.21:14 25:14]]), frequently in Sir. ;] 1. properly, the act of giving: [[philippians 4 15|Php.4:15.]] 2. Objectively, a gift: [[james 1 17|Jas.1:17.]]† SYN.: see: δόμα (AS)
δότης, -ου, ὁ (δίδωμι), [in LXX: [[proverbs 22 8|Pro.22:8]] * ;] = δοτήρ, a giver: [[2-corinthians 9 7|2Co.9:7]] (LXX) (not elsewhere).† (AS)
δουλαγωγέω, -ῶ (δοῦλος, ἄγω), to make a slave, bring into bondage: [[1-corinthians 9 27|1Co.9:27]] (Cremer, 703).† (AS)

δουλεία (T, -λία), -ας, ἡ (δουλεύω), [in LXX, as [[exodus 13 3|Exo.13:3]], for עֶבֶד and cognates ;] slavery, bondage: [[romans 8 15|Rom.8:15, 21]] [[galatians 4 24|Gal.4:24 5:1]], [[hebrews 2 15|Heb.2:15]].† (AS)

Χριστῷ, [[romans 14 18|Rom.14:18]], [[colossians 3 24|Col.3:24]]; νόμῳ θεοῦ, [[romans 7 25|Rom.7:25;]] τ. θεοῖς, [[galatians 4 8|Gal.4:8;]] τ. καιρῷ, [[romans 12 11|Rom.12:11]] (R, mg. for κυρίῳ); ἀλλήλοις, [[galatians 5 13|Gal.5:13;]] σὺν ἐμοί [[philippians 2 22|Php.2:22;]] τ. ἁμαρτίᾳ, [[romans 6 6|Rom.6:6;]] νόμῳ ἁμαρτίας, [[romans 7 25|Rom.7:25;]] ἐπιθυμίαις κ. ἡδοναις, [[titus 3 3|Tit.3:3;]] τ. κοιλία, [[romans 16 18|Rom.16:18;]] μαμωνᾷ, [[matthew 6 24|Mat.6:24]], [[luke 16 13|Luk.16:13]]; τ. στοιχείοις τ, κόσμου, [[galatians 4 9|Gal.4:9]] (Cremer, 217).† (AS)
